MANAGEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Management Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of January 5, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Clearwater Dental Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Manager"), and Clearwater Family Dentistry, P.C., an Arizona professional corporation owned by licensed dentists ("Practice").

1. Engagement. Practice engages Manager to provide the administrative and business services described in this Agreement. Manager provides no dental or other clinical services, and nothing in this Agreement gives Manager any ownership interest in Practice.

2. Clinical Matters. Practice and its licensed professionals have sole and exclusive authority over all clinical decisions, including diagnosis, treatment, referrals, the selection of dental equipment and supplies, and how many patients a dentist sees. Manager will not interfere with the professional judgment of any dentist or hygienist.

3. Manager's Services. Manager will provide the following non-clinical services: billing and collections; payroll and bookkeeping; purchasing of office supplies; scheduling software and other information technology; marketing; the office space and equipment described in Exhibit A; and the front-office staff, whom Manager employs.

4. Clinical Staff. Practice alone hires, supervises, schedules, credentials and terminates its dentists, hygienists and dental assistants, and sets their compensation. Manager employs only non-clinical staff.

5. Patient Records. Practice owns and controls all patient records. Manager will maintain the record system as Practice directs, will not determine the content of any record, and will return the records to Practice in a usable form when this Agreement ends.

6. Billing and Payers. Manager will bill and collect in the name of Practice and as its agent, and will deposit all collections in an account owned by Practice. Coding decisions are made by Practice. Practice decides whether to enter into, renew or end any contract with a payer, and on what terms; Manager may advise but may not sign for Practice.

7. Management Fee. Practice will pay Manager a management fee of $45,000 per month, which the parties have set at the fair market value of the services and which does not vary with Practice's revenue or the volume of patients. The fee is invoiced on the first day of each month and due within 15 days. The parties will review it once a year, and any change must be in a signed writing.

8. Term. This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for ten years. It renews for successive five-year terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 180 days before the term ends.

9. Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement if the other materially breaches it and does not cure the breach within 60 days after written notice. Practice may terminate it immediately if Manager's conduct puts the license of any dentist at risk. On termination, Manager will return the patient records, give Practice a final accounting within 30 days, and continue the services for up to 90 days at Practice's request so that patients are not disrupted. Sections 5, 10 and 11 survive termination.

10. Confidentiality and Patient Information. Each party will keep the other's non-public business information confidential. Manager will handle patient information only as the parties' business associate agreement allows.

11. Indemnification and Liability. Each party will indemnify the other against third-party claims caused by its own negligence or breach of this Agreement. Neither party will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential damages, and Manager's total liability under this Agreement will not exceed the management fees paid in the twelve months before the claim.

12. General. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Arizona, and the state courts located in Maricopa County, Arizona have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising under it. If a change in law makes any part of this Agreement unlawful, the parties will amend it in good faith to keep the arrangement lawful. It may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties.
